definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To restore a friendly relationship; to bring back or return to harmony.
(transitive) To make things compatible or consistent.

quote.citation: 1711 May, [Alexander Pope], An Essay on Criticism, London:  […]  W[illiam] Lewis […]; and sold by W[illiam] Taylor […], T[homas] Osborn[e] […], and J[ohn] Graves […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Some Figures monstrous and mis-shap'd appear, Consider'd singly, or beheld too near, Which, but proportion'd to their Light, or Place, Due Distance reconciles to Form and Grace

quote.citation: 1693, [John Locke], “§2015”, in Some Thoughts Concerning Education, London:  […]  A[wnsham] and J[ohn] Churchill, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: The great men among the ancients understood how to reconcile manual labour with affairs of state.

definitions.definition: (accounting, transitive) To make the net difference in credits and debits of a financial account agree with the balance.
